title: How APIs Create Growth by Inverting the Firm
authors: Seth  G. Benzell; Jonathan Samuel Hersh; Marshall Van Alstyne
eligible_reason: Staggered adoption of public APIs (ProgrammableWeb) by Compustat firms, firm-quarter panel 2007Q1-2020Q3. Table 1 (6 columns) is static TWFE reghdfe ln_mkt_val api_treat_post, absorb(gvkey date), no controls; Figure 5 is an unstacked fully saturated event study with firm and quarter FE; Table 5 column 7 is an OLS firm/quarter FE regression of log breach size on a binary 0-2-years-post indicator (switch-off handled by dropping later treated periods). 179 adopters with 50 distinct adoption quarters, 4,569 never-treated firms. Data shipped.
design_notes: Stata reghdfe/xtreg (programs/2_stata_regressions.do) plus R for gsynth (Table 2, Fig 6), Roth pretrends (Fig A22, 6_pretrends.R). Table 4 adds log total assets; Table A9 adds API-intensity interactions; Table A10 restricts to low-engagement APIs; Table A3/Fig A3 internal-API event study uses a proprietary file not shipped; Table A4 Goodman-Bacon decomposition (ddtiming).
n_adoption_cohorts_note: 179 adopting firms with 50 distinct adoption quarters (2005-2019); 105 firms in 42 cohorts adopt after their first observed quarter; 74 firms adopted at or before entering the panel (always-treated). Table 5 sample (pre-2016): 148 adopters, 41 cohorts with pre-periods.
modern_estimator_note: Reports Goodman-Bacon decomposition (diagnostic), gsynth synthetic control, and Roth (2022) pretrend power; none admitted as modern DiD.

published_estimates.note: Reported as exponentiated 0.998 with t = -0.06 (implied b = -0.002, se about 0.033).
